title: Coinbase Urges Early Work on Bitcoin’s Post-Quantum Transition
source_used: The Quantum Insider (report on a Coinbase blog post, 13 Oct 2026)
key_facts: Coinbase, the cryptocurrency exchange and custodian, published a blog post saying Bitcoin should begin preparing for quantum computing threats before a machine able to break its cryptography is announced.
Coinbase says it holds about 5% of all bitcoin in existence and is preparing its own systems and talking to Bitcoin developers and researchers.
It calls the migration a complex, multiyear undertaking, because changes to Bitcoin's shared rules and the movement of funds can take years.

It wants designs that hide public keys until needed, avoid spending routes open to quantum attack, and let different quantum-resistant signature systems be added later; it points to proposals P2MR (Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 360) and P2TRv2.

It calls for a reproducible, Bitcoin-specific evaluation of candidates including ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and FN-DSA (when standardized) and the compact candidate SHRINCS, and warns that stateful signature systems can allow forgery if a signing state is reused.
Coinbase says the post is an input to an open discussion, not a final position, and it sets no migration deadline and announces no agreed Bitcoin upgrade.
On abandoned or inaccessible coins, it says the debate can continue alongside technical work and lists freezes, spending limits and rescue mechanisms only as options to evaluate.
quote_evidence: Coinbase says Bitcoin should begin preparing for quantum computing threats before a machine capable of breaking its cryptography is announced.
The company said it holds about 5% of all bitcoin in existence, giving it a substantial stake in how the network approaches the problem.
Coinbase presented these as options for evaluation, not settled recommendations.
why_it_matters_hint: Bitcoin's spending security rests on digital signatures that a future quantum computer could defeat, and one of its largest custodians wants the fix started early.
notes: Coinbase's own blog post is the primary source (listed in Google News on 13 Oct 2026); The Block and CoinDesk also covered it. Facts here come from The Quantum Insider's full report. This is a position paper, not a protocol change.
